articles.title: Illinois woman gets orange soda from gas station soda fountain. Then she sees what else came with it: ‘Imagine you got a Coke'
articles.summary: 'Y'all would be surprised how nasty those fountains are!'
articles.body:
Shay (@shayshontez.music), a musician in Illinois, walked into a gas station for a fountain drink. When she walked out, she ended up filming the cup instead of sipping on it.

The reason, she says, is because of some unidentified specks that appeared to float in her drink. Her commenters say she avoided drinking a soda crawling with pests.

As of this writing, Shay's video has more than 57,000 views.

"Y'all, I came in here to get something to drink," she says at the top of the clip. "Look at this. Look at this [expletive]."

The camera leaves her face and drops to the fountain-a row of nozzles above a price board reading 44 oz for $2.29, 52 oz for $2.49, 99-cent refills-then settles on the cup with specks in it.

She's disgusted, but she never says on camera what the specks are. Some viewers guessed they were ants that had found their way into the syrup lines.

Her caption carries the verdict: "Imagine if I drank this," trailed by two nauseated faces and #gasstation. Her account doesn't say whether the specks came off the ice, the syrup lines, or the nozzle. She only adds that she noticed them before the first sip.

"Imagine you got a Coke," one commenter said. Shay replied, "I swear. Good thing I don't like dark soda."

One woman could suddenly understand why her husband avoids dispensed beverages. "And now I see the reason why my husband doesn't do fountain drinks at all!" she wrote.

"Literally takes an extra 5 mins at the end of a shift to take the nozzles off and soak them overnight then a wipe down and it stays clean," a third person commented. "Y'all would be surprised how nasty those fountains are!"

There are no gray areas for self-serve fountains under Illinois rules. The state's Food Code defines a "Food Establishment" as an operation that "stores, prepares, packages, serves, [and] vends food directly to the consumer," which is what a gas-station soda counter does. That puts it under the same sanitation law as any restaurant.

Illinois adopted the 2022 FDA Food Code, whose pest provisions are clear. It says that insects, rodents, and other pests must be "controlled to minimize their presence within food establishments." Nozzles, ice bins, and syrup lines are the spots inspectors flag when they go uncleaned.

Catching it falls to local government, not the state. The Illinois Department of Public Health says such businesses are "regulated by local health departments serving the jurisdiction where the establishment is located," so a cup like Shay's is a complaint for the county health department. It can inspect the machine and cite what it finds.

Subplot News reached out to Shay via TikTok message and comment, and to the Illinois Department of Public Health via email for more information.

This story is republished with permission. It originally appeared on Subplot News .

articles.title: Coordenador da campanha de Lula diz que ‘houve boicote’ no transporte em capitais governadas pela oposição ao PT | G1
articles.standfirst: 'Isso não existe numa democracia, o povo tem direito de escolher’, defendeu o senador Camilo Santana (PT).
articles.summary: 'Isso não existe numa democracia, o povo tem direito de escolher’, defendeu o senador Camilo Santana (PT).
articles.body:
O coordenador da campanha de reeleição do presidente Lula (PT), o senador Camilo Santana, disse que “houve um boicote claro nas capitais” governadas pela oposição do PT ao citar a suposta interferência no transporte público ocorrida neste domingo (25), segundo turno das eleições.

“Houve um boicote, claramente, nas capitais, principalmente no Nordeste, que são oposições aos governadores, como Salvador [Bahia] e São Luís [Maranhão]. Boicotaram o transporte público. Isso não existe numa democracia. O povo tem direito de escolher”, declarou.

Para Camilo, a decisão do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) veio tarde, sem conseguir corrigir os efeitos do caos no transporte ocorrido durante todo o dia em cidades como Salvador, São Paulo e São Luís.

“A decisão [de prorrogar a votação em duas horas] é para garantir que as pessoas possam votar. O problema é que saiu depois que elas estavam fechadas. Em muitas sessões, estão cortando o direito de as pessoas votarem”, disse.

O coordenador da campanha de Lula, senador Camilo Santana (PT). — Foto: Divulgação/PT

“Nós vamos avaliar agora, sentar com a coordenação para avaliar”, afirmou.

Santana pontuou que o suposto boicote promovido por prefeitos como Ricardo Nunes (MDB) e Bruno Reis (União Brasil) fere a lisura da eleição no Brasil e a visão que a democracia brasileira tem no exterior.

O comentário foi feito na chegada do coordenador ao Hotel Intercontinental, em São Paulo, onde a equipe da campanha de Lula aguarda a apuração dos votos deste domingo (25).

À TV Globo, o prefeito Ricardo Nunes afirmou, por mensagem, que a frota de ônibus da capital paulista está maior do que a demanda, mas não informou os números. “Nenhum eleitor está sem atendimento na cidade."

O presidente nacional do PT, Edinho Silva, disse na tarde deste domingo (25) que “é muito grave” a tentativa de interferência no processo eleitoral por parte de prefeitos de várias cidades do Brasil ao não disponibilizar a quantidade necessária de ônibus para os eleitores no segundo turno.

Segundo Edinho, a falta de ônibus em capitais como São Paulo e Salvador “só reafirma a manipulação que o PT vem enfrentando desde o início do pleito deste ano".

“É grave o que aconteceu em relação ao transporte no Brasil inteiro. Aqui em São Paulo e na Bahia está caracterizado descumprimento da legislação. Nos outros estados estamos apurando ainda. Mas São Paulo e Bahia descumpriram a legislação. O que é grave, porque quem precisa de transporte público, as pesquisas mostram, é o nosso eleitorado. Isso significa interferir diretamente no processo eleitoral. Só reafirma aquilo que nós enfrentamos a eleição inteira: manipulação das big techs. Na reta final, infelizmente, a gente constata isso”, disse.

Sobre a atuação do prefeito da capital paulista, Ricardo Nunes (MDB), e do prefeito de Salvador, Bruno Soares Reis (União Brasil), Edinho afirmou que cometeram crimes e devem ser punidos pela lei eleitoral.

“A lei existe para ser cumprida. Quando a legislação estabelece a garantia de direito de transporte ao eleitor, penso que ela deve ser cumprida. Quem descumpre a lei está cometendo um crime e está interferindo no processo eleitoral”, declarou.

A declaração foi dada na chegada do petista ao Hotel Intercontinental, na região dos Jardins, Centro de São Paulo, onde a campanha de Lula (PT) aguarda o resultado da apuração do 2° turno da corrida eleitoral.

“Espero que a gente aprenda com esse processo eleitoral no Brasil e a gente corrija. Porque os erros são graves."

Sobre a atuação do presidente do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), Kássio Nunes Marques, Edinho apontou:

“Não quero falar sobre ministros agora. Só quero que o TSE faça cumprir a legislação. Nós não fechamos o processo ainda. Há muito o que fazer até o dia da posse. Quero continuar acreditando que as instituições brasileiras vão sair fortalecidas desse processo. E que a democracia sai fortalecida, que a gente aprenda com tudo o que está acontecendo agora”, afirmou.

O ministro Cristiano Zanin, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), determinou a prorrogação do horário de encerramento de votação até as 19h deste domingo (25) após os relatos de redução de frota de ônibus em diversas cidades do país. A decisão vale para todas as seções eleitorais do Brasil .

Na capital e na Grande São Paulo, houve registros de ônibus enfileirados parados nas ruas, garagens lotadas de coletivos, demora na circulação , pontos e terminais lotados e passageiros que relatam longas esperas.

Essa dinâmica aconteceu mesmo após a Justiça Eleitoral determinar que a Prefeitura de São Paulo e a SPTrans mantivesse 100% da frota em operação neste domingo (25), em níveis equivalentes aos de dias úteis.

A decisão foi dada após pedido da coligação do candidato Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), que protocolou uma petição com pedido de liminar de urgência, no Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), solicitando a prorrogação do horário de encerramento da votação em municípios atingidos por problemas no transporte público.

A solicitação abrange pelo menos nove estados: São Paulo, Alagoas, Pernambuco, Roraima, Piauí, Paraíba, Pará, Paraná e Rio de Janeiro.

A campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) também solicitou a prorrogação por duas horas em municípios de Minas Gerais e do Rio Grande do Sul, atingidos por fortes chuvas.

A campanha pediu que a extensão fosse aplicada em: Belo Horizonte, Poços de Caldas e municípios da Região Metropolitana de Belo Horizonte, além de São Borja, Itaqui e Uruguaiana, no Rio Grande do Sul, atingidas por chuvas e pela cheia do rio Uruguai.

No Terminal Varginha, extremo sul da capital, moradores disseram ter aguardado até três horas por um ônibus. Em Santana, Zona Norte, e na região do Jardim Ângela, Zona Sul, também foram registrados passageiros em filas à espera de transporte. Na Vila Zilda, na Zona Norte, há relatos de motoristas que se recusaram a levar moradores aos locais de votação.

Pessoas que passaram de carro pelo entorno do Terminal Santana, por exemplo, encontraram ônibus parados e passageiros à espera de transporte público em meio à chuva. Diante da situação, um casal decidiu oferecer caronas a quem precisava se deslocar.

Ônibus parados na garagem em Santana, na Zona Norte de SP. — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Em entrevista ao g1 , uma pessoa que preferiu não se identificar, contou que saiu de casa com a intenção de ajudar passageiros, após notícias sobre a circulação de poucos ônibus e devido às chuvas.

“Quando chegamos próximos ao Terminal Santana, vimos muitas filas e ônibus parados, sem prestar serviço. Passamos por volta das 14h30”, relatou.

Segundo o entrevistado, chovia bastante no momento em que o casal passou pelo local (veja vídeo acima) .

Durante o trajeto, uma senhora contou que precisava votar no bairro Jaçanã. O casal perguntou se ela precisava de carona, mas percebeu que ela e outras pessoas estavam receosas em aceitar a oferta.

“Minha esposa saiu pelo terminal, perguntamos a muita gente, mas o receio de aceitar ficou nítido”, afirmou.

Na Estrada M'Boi Mirim, na altura do número 4.017, por volta das 13h, passageiros ficaram sob chuva aguardando transporte nos pontos de ônibus por mais de 40 minutos.

articles.title: Celina Leão é eleita governadora do DF: 'Vou governar para todos' | G1
articles.standfirst: Com 100% das seções apuradas, Celina Leão teve 57,18% dos votos válidos no 2º turno na disputa pelo governo do DF.
articles.summary: Celina Leão é eleita governadora do DF com  57,18% dos votos válidos no segundo turno e afirma que pretende governar para toda a população da capital.
articles.body:
Celina Leão ( PP ) fez sua primeira declaração pública após vencer a disputa pelo governo do Distrito Federal, neste domingo (25). A candidata derrotou Leandro Grass (PT) no 2º turno e foi eleita para comandar o Palácio do Buriti pelos próximos quatro anos.

Em seu primeiro discurso após a vitória, Celina agradeceu a Deus e aos eleitores e afirmou que pretende governar para toda a população do DF, incluindo quem não votou nela.

“Quero agradecer primeiro a Deus. A Ele toda honra e toda glória. Agradecer a cada um que confiou na gente. Tenho certeza de que estamos prontas para servir esta cidade. Eu falava durante toda a campanha sobre o coração do servo, que é o coração do rei. Nós vamos servir esta cidade com humildade", declarou a governadora.

A governadora disse ainda que já foi cumprimentada pelo adversário, Leandro Grass, por telefone. Ela também destacou a presença de mulheres nos cargos majoritários e agradeceu à imprensa e à senadora Michelle Bolsonaro.

Celina Leão (PP), governadora reeleita do Distrito Federal, em primeiro discurso após a vitória — Foto: TV Globo/Reprodução

Disse ainda estar confiante na vitória de Flávio Bolsonaro na disputa presidencial.

Com 100% das seções apuradas, Celina Leão teve 57,18% (987.142 votos válidos). Leandro Grass (PT) teve 42,82% (739.130 votos válidos).

Celina Leão, candidata ao governo do DF, vota no 2º turno — Foto: TV Globo/Reprodução

"Nós somos o único estado da Federação que tem os quatro cargos majoritários compostos por mulheres. Esse é um grande desafio nosso. Vamos honrar a população trabalhando, servindo e fazendo desta capital, deste estado, um modelo para o Brasil", indicou Celina Leão.

A governadora seguiu para o comitê de campanha, no Setor de Indústria e Abastecimento (SIA), para agradecer, segundo ela, “a todas as pessoas que estavam nas ruas e que estão lá acompanhando”.

"E agradecer a cada um aqui do Distrito Federal. Você que votou, você que não votou, nós vamos governar para todos", finalizou a governadora.

Durante a campanha de segundo turno, a candidata afirmou que parte do eleitorado teria se confundido na hora de votar e, por isso, passou a reforçar o número 11.

Mais de 26 mil eleitores digitaram 22 para governador, número do PL, embora não houvesse candidato ao GDF com essa numeração. No entanto, os dados eleitorais não permitem saber em quem essas pessoas pretendiam votar.

🔎Ou seja: os votos anulados por quem digitou 22 seriam mais que suficientes para elegê-la, caso a intenção fosse, realmente, escolher Celina Leão.

Além de reforçar o próprio número, Celina manteve a ampla aliança partidária formada no primeiro turno e buscou novas adesões.

Entre os apoios recebidos estão o do ex-candidato Kiko Caputo (Novo) e o da ex-governadora Maria de Lourdes Abadia (PSD). A agenda da candidata também incluiu caminhadas, reuniões comunitárias e encontros com moradores, lideranças e apoiadores.

De acordo com a campanha de Celina, o segundo turno foi marcado pela ampliação do diálogo com os eleitores e pela apresentação mais detalhada das propostas.

A candidata manteve agendas nas ruas e passou a reforçar especialmente projetos para saúde, educação e transporte.

Na reta final, a estratégia foi intensificar a presença junto aos eleitores e buscar o voto de quem ainda estava indeciso.

A campanha afirma ainda que procura adaptar o diálogo às demandas das diferentes regiões do DF. "A prioridade é manter essa presença, esclarecer dúvidas e conquistar a confiança de quem ainda está decidindo o voto. Não existe eleição ganha", destaca um assessor.

articles.title: Imprensa internacional repercute prolongamento da votação no Brasil | G1
articles.standfirst: Conflito de horários entre decisões da Justiça Eleitoral e o fechamento das urnas no Brasil ganhou destaque em jornais pelo mundo.
articles.summary: Conflito de horários entre decisões da Justiça Eleitoral e o fechamento das urnas no Brasil ganhou destaque em jornais pelo mundo.
articles.body:
O jornal português Público destacou a prorrogação da votação na capa de seu site. — Foto: Reprodução: Público.

Jornais e sites de notícias de países ao redor do mundo noticiaram a extensão dos horário de votação nos colégios eleitoriais do Brasil, após o Supremo Tribunal Federal atender a pedidos das campanhas de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e Flávio Bolsonaro (PL).

O ministro Cristiano Zanin determinou a extensão da votação até as 19h em todo o país após denúncias de problemas no transporte de eleitores pelo país e as fortes chuvas que afetam várias regiões do Brasil.

No exterior, veículos de comunicação na Europa e nas Américas dedicaram linhas do tempo de notícias em tempo real para acompanhar a apuração.

Em Portugal, o jornal de maior circulação Público dedicou o maior destaque de sua capa ao imbroglio nas eleições brasileiras. Já o argentino Clarín destacou que o horário da expedição da decisão de prorrogamento aconteceu no mesmo horário de fechamento das urnas.

O jornal argentino Clarín destacou que o conflito de horários entre as decisões dos juízes — Foto: Reprodução: Clarín

Já o americano The New York Times destacou que, apesar da prorrogação do horário de votação em todo o país, ainda não estava claro se eleitores que chegaram aos locais de votação a tempo porque algumas seções eleitorais já haviam encerrado suas atividades.

A imprensa internacional repercutiu neste domingo (25) a votação no 2º turno das eleições presidenciais brasileiras.

As manchetes destacaram a importância que o resultado do pleito no Brasil terá para a América Latina e para o mundo. Veja abaixo.

O El País, da Espanha, afirmou que o Brasil decidirá entre "entregar todo o poder aos Bolsonaro ou dar uma última vitória a Lula";

A Associated Press, dos Estados Unidos, chamou de "decisão tensa" a votação deste domingo;

O New York Times, dos Estados Unidos, afirmou que "Flávio pode conseguir a maior vitória da direita da América Latina";

O The Guardian, do Reino Unido, disse que o resultado da eleição é "altamente imprevisível".

O El País, da Espanha, afirmou que o Brasil decidirá entre "entregar todo o poder aos Bolsonaro ou dar uma última vitória a Lula".

A fala é uma alusão ao fato de o Congresso brasileiro ter se tornado mais conservador após o 1º turno, com uma expansão da bancada do PL, que agora é o partido com a maior bancada em ambas as casas legislativas.

Eleger o senador Flávio Bolsonaro, herdeiro de um golpista e de uma dinastia ultraconservadora que engoliu a direita tradicional, significa transformá-lo no presidente mais poderoso das últimas décadas, porque ele comandaria o governo federal, controlaria o Congresso com uma maioria recorde e moldaria o Supremo Tribunal Federal", escreveu.

O jornal disse ainda que uma vitória de Lula significaria "manter o rumo político e econômico, apostar, nestes tempos tão turbulentos, em um mundo regido por regras e em um líder com credenciais democráticas consolidadas".

A reportagem disse também que "brasileiros de esquerda e direita se mobilizaram em massa nas últimas semanas de campanha em busca dos votos que vão decidir as eleições mais acirradas de suas vidas".

A agência de notícias norte-americana Associated Press deu destaque ao elemento de tensão que cerca a votação deste domingo.

"Brasileiros votam em uma disputa tensa entre Lula e Bolsonaro com influência dos EUA e com a América Latina em jogo. (...) O resultado determinará se os Estados Unidos ampliarão significativamente sua crescente influência na América Latina", afirmou a agência.

A reportagem citou uma pesquisa do Datafolha desta semana que mostrou Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro apareceram com 50% da intenção de voto. Também afirmou que "a diferença entre os dois candidatos é marcante":

"Uma vitória de Bolsonaro representaria uma guinada à direita do país mais populoso e da maior economia da América Latina, em um ano com vitórias de aliados de Trump [na região]. (...) Uma vitória de Lula manteria o Brasil e o México sob a liderança de políticos de centro-esquerda", afirmou.

O jornal "The New York Times" afirmou que "Flávio pode conquistar a maior vitória da direita da América Latina" e também repercutiu o quão acirrada está a disputa neste segundo turno.

"Os brasileiros vão às urnas neste domingo para eleger um novo presidente em uma eleição disputada ferozmente [entre Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro], no que representa o maior teste até agora para a direita em ascensão que vem conquistando presidências em toda a América Latina (...) Uma vitória de Bolsonaro representaria a maior conquista até agora de um movimento de direita em ascensão que avança por toda a América Latina", afirmou a reportagem.

O veículo norte-americano também citou o grande interesse do governo Trump no pleito — o presidente dos EUA tem afinidade ideológica com Flávio.

O jornal britânico "The Guardian" afirmou que o pleito brasileiro é "altamente imprevisível" e destacou que a distância entre os dois candidatos é a menor da história para um 2º turno na disputa pela presidência.

A reportagem disse que Lula "tenta uma volta por cima sem precedentes" contra Flávio, e citou a "vitória surpreendente" do bolsonarista no 1º turno.

"A diferença entre eles foi a menor já registrada em um primeiro turno, inferior a 2% dos votos. O presidente, de 81 anos, passou boa parte da campanha do segundo turno concentrado em estimular o comparecimento às urnas (...) e em alimentar temores sobre o que significaria o retorno ao poder de um integrante da família Bolsonaro".

O jornal também citou que Flávio pretende dar um indulto a seu pai, Jair Bolsonaro, caso seja eleito e que ele prometeu mudar a Constituição brasileira.

articles.title: Após STF prorrogar votação, mesários não recebem orientação e parte das escolas são fechadas em SP; eleitores podem ficar sem votar | G1
articles.standfirst: Ministro Cristiano Zanin determinou que votação em todo o país se estenda até as 19h deste domingo (25) após problemas no transporte público, mas urnas já haviam sido recolhidas em diversas escolas na capital paulista.
articles.summary: Ministro Cristiano Zanin determinou que votação em todo o país se estenda até as 19h deste domingo (25) após problemas no transporte público, mas urnas já haviam sido recolhidas em diversas escolas na capital paulista.
articles.body:
No Colégio Fidelino de Figueiredo, na Rua Imaculada Conceição, mesários foram orientados a permanecer no local. Urnas já foram recolhidas. — Foto: Reprodução

Mesários de zonas eleitorais da cidade de São Paulo relataram falta de informações sobre como proceder após o ministro Cristiano Zanin, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), determinar a prorrogação do horário de votação até as 19h deste domingo (25) .

Em unidades da região central, segundo relatos, as urnas já haviam sido recolhidas e os mesários dispensados antes de receberem novas orientações .

Após decisão de prorrogar a votação até as 19h, as urnas que já haviam sido fechadas não podem ser reabertas.

Segundo o Tribunal Superiror Eleitoral (TSE), 1.225 seções eleitorais em todo o Brasil chegaram a ter votos para presidente apurados . O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) aparece com 57,66%, com 193.574 votos. O senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) aparece com 42,34%, com 142.169 votos.

A medida ocorreu depois de diversos municipios registrarem problemas no transporte público. Na capital e na Grande São Paulo, houve registros de ônibus enfileirados parados nas ruas, garagens lotadas de coletivos, demora na circulação , pontos e terminais lotados e passageiros que relatam longas esperas.

Em nota, o Tribunal Regional Eleitoral de São Paulo (TRE-SP) afirmou que todas as zonas eleitorais do estado foram informadas sobre a decisão que prorrogou a votação até as 19h em todo o país.

Segundo o tribunal, a determinação está sendo cumprida. Sobre as seções eleitorais que já haviam encerrado os trabalhos, o TRE-SP informou que todos os votos registrados serão computados e totalizados integralmente, sem prejuízo. (leia mais abaixo).

No Colégio Fidelino de Figueiredo, no Centro da capital, porém, a situação é diferente. Ao g1 , uma mesária afirmou que a orientação inicial era encerrar a votação às 17h. Segundo ela, todas as seções do colégio foram fechadas, e os mesários ficaram aguardando informações do cartório eleitoral.

“Nós tínhamos visto, nós, mesários, as informações na internet e aguardamos até as 17h. Quando deu 17h, perguntamos, e a pessoa responsável por aqui falou: 'Fechou, fechou'. E orientou para que todos fechassem [as urnas]”, relatou.

De acordo com a mesária, as urnas já haviam sido recolhidas e as cabines, desmontadas. Os mesários e presidentes de seção, porém, foram orientados a permanecer na escola enquanto aguardavam novas instruções.

“Não estão deixando ninguém sair. Mas não dá para saber se há eleitores para votar, porque estamos trancados no colégio”, disse.

Em outra unidade, na Universidade Anhembi Morumbi, na Mooca, um mesário informou que a votação continuava, mas que uma urna já havia sido fechada.

Segundo o relato, o cartório eleitoral orientou que, caso um eleitor chegasse a uma seção cuja votação já tivesse sido encerrada, a intenção de votar fosse registrada em ata . Os procedimentos de encerramento deveriam continuar, mas os documentos não poderiam ser guardados no envelope até segunda ordem.

A Justiça Eleitoral prevê procedimentos de contingência para lidar com problemas técnicos nas urnas eletrônicas e falhas operacionais durante a votação e a apuração. Segundo o TSE, as medidas podem incluir a substituição da urna ou de componentes e, em último caso, a realização de votação manual, com cédulas de papel.

As regras disponíveis no site do tribunal, porém, tratam de falhas técnicas e operacionais e não esclarecem como proceder no caso de seções encerradas antes do horário determinado por decisão judicial.

Boletim de urna da EMEI Professora Zilda de Franceschi, na Vila Madalena. Urnas foram fechadas às 17h. — Foto: Reprodução

Confira a situação de alguns locais de votação, até as 18h, segundo apuração do g1 e TV Globo:

Escola Shinquichi Agari, Zona Leste de SP

Estadual Luzia de Queiroz Oliveira, Zona Leste de SP

EMEI Francisca Julia da Silva, Zona Sul de SP

Em frente da EMEF Emiliano Di Cavalcanti, na Zona Leste de São Paulo, uma eleitora afirmou que aguarda por mais de uma hora a reabertura dos portões.

"Estou aqui em um horário válido de votação, que foi estendido, e já faz mais de 1 hora que falaram que a escola iria reabrir para votar, e ainda não abriu".

Em imagens obtidas pela TV Globo, é possível contar ao menos 12 pessoas em frente ao portão fechado do local.

Na EMEI Francisca Julia da Silva, região do Jardim Ângela, Zona Sul de São Paulo, uma eleitora relatou que aguardava a liberação para votar, mas que a equipe de mesários estava indo embora.

A decisão de prorrogar a votação foi tomada por Zanin após um pedido apresentado pela coligação do candidato Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), que solicitou a extensão do horário em municípios afetados por problemas no transporte público.

A campanha do candidato à Presidência da Repúblcia Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) seguiu a campanha do adversário, neste domingo (25), e também solicitou ao Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) que prorrogue por duas horas o horário de votação. A campanha pediu que a extensão fosse aplicada em cidades de Minas Gerais e Rio Grande do Sul.

O pedido foi protocolado no Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) e no STF. Inicialmente, a solicitação abrangia municípios de pelo menos nove estados, entre eles São Paulo. A decisão de Zanin, no entanto, determinou a prorrogação em todo o país.

Na determinação, o ministro estabeleceu que o recebimento dos votos fosse estendido por duas horas, até as 19h, no horário de Brasília.

“Considerando a gravidade dos fatos narrados, que chegaram ao conhecimento do Supremo Tribunal Federal em 16:32:49, da data de hoje, e diante da urgência evidente na medida, determino prorrogação por duas horas, até às 19h, horário de Brasília, do encerramento do recebimento dos votos em todas as seções de todo o Brasil, cabendo ao TSE dar cumprimento”, escreveu.

Com a decisão, a totalização dos votos, que já havia começado, foi paralisada.

Até a última atualização desta reportagem, não havia informação sobre quantos eleitores poderiam ter sido prejudicados pelo encerramento antecipado das seções relatadas pelos mesários.

"O Tribunal Regional Eleitoral de São Paulo (TRE-SP) informa que, em cumprimento à decisão proferida pelo Ministro Cristiano Zanin, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), determinando a prorrogação do horário de votação até as 19h em todo o território nacional, todas as Zonas Eleitorais do Estado foram cientificadas a respeito. A determinação está sendo cumprida.

Quanto às seções eleitorais que já encerraram os trabalhos de votação, o TRE-SP esclarece que todos os respectivos votos registrados serão regular e integralmente computados e totalizados, sem prejuízo.

Des. José Antonio Encinas Manfré, Presidente do Tribunal Regional Eleitoral de Sã o Paulo."

articles.title: Dead whale found washed up on Flimby beach in storm
articles.summary: People are asked to keep away from the juvenile northern bottlenose whale on Flimby beach.
articles.body:
People have been warned to keep away from a dead whale which has washed up on a shoreline.

Maryport Coastguard Rescue Team said it was called to Flimby beach where a juvenile northern bottlenose whale was found on Saturday, after Storm Austen and Storm Boelo battered the UK.

Northern bottlenose whales are most commonly found in the North Atlantic Ocean, where they can dive to more than 1,400m (4,593ft) deep and stay submerged for up to two hours, according to the charity Whale and Dolphin Conservation.

The Coastguard urged people to not touch the carcass as it "may have toxins that can pass to humans" and advised people to take care as Storm Boelo was "still going strong".

The Coastguard asked people to report any sightings of stranded whales as soon as possible, even if they might be dead, to keep clear from the mammal and to wait for help.

"Gathering round the animal will intensify their distress, and it is possible for disease to be passed to humans," it added.

articles.title: Body found in search for man who fell overboard from ferry
articles.summary: Formal identification is yet to take place but the family of 82-year-old Jim Wither has been informed.
articles.body:
The body of a missing ferry passenger who fell overboard has been found on a beach in North Ayrshire.

HM Coastguard responded to a report of a man going overboard from the MV Caledonian Isles near Arran about 20:30 on Sunday 18 October.

The man was later named as 82-year-old Jim Wither, who was reported missing from Johnstone, Renfrewshire.

Police Scotland earlier received a report that the body of a man had been found in the Largs beach area on Sunday. Formal identification has yet to take place, but the family of Jim Wither has been informed.

Two helicopters, a coastguard aircraft, Royal National Lifeboat Institution (RNLI) lifeboats and rescue teams from the surrounding area were sent to find the passenger, but the search was called off at 16:55 on Monday.

Officers said the death was not being treated as suspicious and a report would be submitted to the procurator fiscal in due course.

articles.title: Cornell fraternity member seeks dismissal from Jane Doe’s sexual assault lawsuit
articles.summary: An attorney for Diego Sarabia said his client isn’t accused of taking part in the alleged assault and should be excluded from the case.
articles.body:
One of the men sued by a former Cornell University student identified as Jane Doe has asked a judge to dismiss the claims against him, arguing that her allegations do not support her broader accusations of rape and sexual assault.

Diego Sarabia filed the motion Friday seeking dismissal of all claims against him in the lawsuit Doe filed Sept. 16 in New York state court. Sarabia, who was a member of the Chi Phi fraternity, was one of seven men originally sued by Doe for allegedly participating in a gang rape at the Chi Phi house from Oct. 19 to 20, 2024.

Sarabia denies the allegations against him, according to the filing. His attorneys argue that even if the complaint's factual allegations are accepted as true for the purposes of the motion, the claims against him were filed too late, are legally insufficient, or both.

James C. Knox, an attorney for Sarabia, wrote in the motion that as far as the allegations against his client, "this is essentially a lawsuit about a forced kiss." Knox argued that the conduct Doe attributed to Sarabia did not qualify for the extended statute of limitations she cited for certain sexual offenses.

Doe accused Sarabia of grabbing her face, kissing her and snorting ketamine off her body with other fraternity members during a drug- and alcohol-fueled encounter in what was known as the "alumni room" of the fraternity house.

"Throughout a sprawling complaint approaching 600 paragraphs, plaintiff repeatedly, collectively and without differentiation accuses seven student defendants of 'sexual assault and rape,'" Knox wrote in his filing. "Those legally conclusory statements do not substitute for pleaded facts."

Knox argued that the complaint did not allege that Sarabia "supplied her with drugs or alcohol, participated in any of the alleged sexual encounters described elsewhere in the complaint, or was even present for most of the conduct that forms the basis of plaintiff's broader allegations."

The attorney said that the assault, battery and intentional infliction of emotional distress claims were barred by a one-year statute of limitations and the allegations against Sarabia did not qualify for extensions cited in the complaint.

Doe's attorney Thomas Giuffra declined to comment on Sunday. Giuffra previously agreed to withdraw claims against the acting president of the fraternity's chapter at the time.

The lawsuit inspired calls for a reckoning at the Ivy League institution, where past and current students and community members have accused the administration of not doing enough to protect women from sexual assault.

Cornell's Board of Trustees hired former Deputy Attorney General Sally Yates "to lead a comprehensive independent review of how the University prevents and responds to sexual harassment, sexual assault and related misconduct on campus."

Doe's allegations were investigated by Cornell University Police. An internal civil rights investigation led to the expulsion of two students and disciplinary action against others. Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten declined to bring charges in November 2024 based on a six-page statement in which Doe described some of the sexual conduct that night as consensual.

Van Houten declined to evaluate other investigative materials that had been gathered by investigators, including other witness statements.

Gov. Kathy Hochul called the evaluation inadequate and recently appointed state Attorney General Letitia James as special prosecutor to investigate the allegations. James' office has started that process. The attorney general is expected to hire outside investigators to assist with the effort.

Two of the accused men are seeking to disqualify James from overseeing the investigation based on a comment she made on social media about the case before she was tapped to run the probe. They argued the state's top law enforcement official had prejudged the case. Both challenges are still pending.

James has deflected calls to step down from the case and has said she is "committed to leading a comprehensive investigation they can trust, guided only by the facts, the evidence, and the law."

articles.title: EPFO considers Rs 25,000cr war chest to stabilise interest payouts
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation is discussing a dedicated Rs 25,000-crore Interest Stabilisation Reserve, designed to insulate the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation is discussing a dedicated Rs 25,000-crore Interest Stabilisation Reserve, designed to insulate the annual interest payouts of its nearly 30 crore members from the turbulence caused by corporate bond defaults and forced-exit losses.Officials said EPFO and government want a stable regime for its subscribers and wish to avoid any sharp fall or spike in rates due to market conditions or defaults.Under existing regulatory frameworks, credit losses and exit haircuts, resulting from downgraded securities, directly impact EPFO’s interest account and depress the annual interest rate for members.Report on ISR sent to panel studying EPFO investment frameworkA proposal submitted by IIM Kozhikode, which among other things studied the feasibility of creating an Interest Stabilisation Reserve (ISR), was discussed in detail by EPFO’s investment committee (IC) Thursday, TOI has learnt.The report has now been sent to a high-poweredJ panel constituted to examine the agency’s investment framework and recognise non-performing investments.The report suggested building the stabilisation reserve progressively via surplus ETF capital gains and excess interest income and investing it strictly in liquid govt securities (G-Secs) to ensure absolute capital safety, sovereign backing, immediate liquidity, and risk-free yield, said persons familiar with the deliberations.The reserve will not only shield subscribers but will also back active exit policies and empower portfolio managers to execute disciplined, multi-year exits from troubled assets without hesitation.The report took into account the current realities of India’s over-the-counter (OTC) corporate bond market, which remains shallow and illiquid, such that when institutional holders such as EPFO are forced to exit distressed assets, thin market depth results in severe haircuts.Historically, EPFO relied heavily on equity ETF capital gains to offset credit stress.The report, however, noted that the volatile market downturn of FY 2019-20 coincided with major credit events like the IL&FS default, which exposed a critical vulnerability.“Credit stress and equity market crashes are highly correlated. Relying solely on ETF gains is dangerous; a standalone prudential reserve is a structural necessity,” it said.The study evaluated absolute worst-case liquidation scenarios across the portfolio netted against available ETF gains, pinpointing a cumulative baseline shortfall of approximately Rs 23,837 crore.“To account for incomplete market data and ensure a bulletproof prudential buffer, the report recommends formalising an ISR Fund of Rs 25,000 crore,” it said.The study also ran a historical back-testing simulation which modelled portfolio returns from 2010-11 to 2023-24, demonstrating that a Rs 25,000-crore baseline successfully absorbs annual shortfalls and stabilises declared interest rates across typical economic cycles.The only exception was 2019-20, where portfolio deficit spiked to Rs 55,640 crore, leading to deep drawdown from the reserve.“However, the subsequent recovery in investment performance in later years indicates that such a shortfall would likely have been temporary in nature.In such a scenario, EPFO could have bridged the temporary deficit through a short-term advance or loan mechanism, which could subsequently be repaid from future surpluses generated during recovery years,” the study said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Former CJI D Y Chandrachud was more deferential to government than needed, says Justice Kaul
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Former CJI D Y Chandrachud was more deferential to the govt than necessary in matters of judicial appointments, former SC judge Justice Sanjay
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former CJI D Y Chandrachud was more deferential to the govt than necessary in matters of judicial appointments, former SC judge Justice Sanjay Kishan Kaul has said in his forthcoming book ‘Without Fear Or Favour’, and claimed that he was prevented from hearing petitions for re-examination of the validity of provisions of PMLA.Kaul also claimed Justice Chandrachud had, allegedly under pressure from govt, withdrawn a case from him in which a bench headed by him had questioned delays in implementation of the SC collegium’s resolutions for appointment of judges. This, he said, “troubled him the most” as the case was assigned years ago and was taken away all of a sudden.Reacting to the claims, Justice Chandrachud said, “There was never even a dissent by any member of the collegium over any name during discussions for appointments to the SC.”‘DYC asked if he should call government on collegium picks’Sources said resolutions passed by the collegium for appointments to the SC during Justice Chandrachud’s tenure were unanimous and signed by all members of the collegium without recording a single dissent.In this case, a bench of Justices Kaul and Sudhanshu Dhulia had pulled up govt for its alleged pick-and-choose policy in clearing names sent by the collegium and had on Nov 20, 2023, asked why Centre was not transferring four judges from Gujarat HC and not appointing two Sikh lawyers for Punjab and Haryana HC as recommended by the collegium. The case was thereafter taken away from his bench and it has not been listed in the last three years.In an interview to Karan Thapar for The Wire, Justice Kaul claimed the former CJI took him aside during a collegium meeting and asked whether he should telephone govt to ascertain its views on the proposed appointments. Justice Kaul said pre-approval from govt before discussions in the collegium was a matter of concern.“This has unfortunately become a practice of names being discussed, and some kind of previous discussion with govt. That used to happen. It has been happening, I think before CJI Chandrachud and after. That is why it troubles me,” he said, adding that there was nothing wrong in holding consultations with govt, but it should happen only after the collegium’s decision and not before.Asked whether Justice Chandrachud was too deferential to govt, Justice Kaul said, “There is a judicial side and there is an administrative side of the Chief Justice of India. I wouldn’t be concerned with the judicial side. I believe he had both the intellectual heft and the capacity and hard work to do so. But in consultations with govt and collaboration, I felt he was more deferential than necessary to carry it forward.”Justice Kaul said he tried to discourage Justice Chandrachud from discussing everything with govt beforehand as it could create its own problems. Asked whether Justice Chandrachud failed to live up to the high expectations from him, Justice Kaul said, “I would say that expectations were higher from him.”TOI has reported how Justice Kaul had vigorously and successfully pushed many names for judgeship as part of the SC and HC collegiums and three of his proposals had met with resistance from other members of the panel. The then CJI had tactically refrained from holding collegium meetings to avoid embarrassing situations.In reply to the TOI article, Justice Kaul had sent a rejoinder and said, “There was no question of insistence of appointment of those suggested by me and all recommendations have been made by consensus. That other collegium members had reservations and I pushed the names, thus, seem to be a flight of your imagination.”Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Serbia's veteran ruler Vučić concedes election to student-led protest movement
articles.summary: The populist right-wing leader of 12 years says it is "clear" his party has lost the vote billed as a referendum on the country's future.
articles.body:
Serbia's long-standing leader Aleksandar Vučić has admitted defeat to the student-led protest movement in snap parliamentary elections.

"We still do not have final results... it is clear that we have lost these elections," the right-wing populist leader said as he conceded late on Sunday.

Preliminary figures provided by Serbia's election commission indicated a record high turnout, which commentators had suggested would favour the student movement.

Vučić had called the snap elections after two years of protests triggered by the 2024 collapse of a train station canopy in the city of Novi Sad, which killed 16 and was seen as emblematic of corruption and negligence in Serbia.

Vučić had spent two terms as president and could not seek a third term, so was leading his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) with the aim of returning to the post of prime minister, which he left in 2017.

The Student List's lead candidate Ilija Srdanović told BBC Serbian: "This will be a free state."

He said the anti-corruption movement, which had attracted anti-government voters across Serbia, hoped to "free the country from tyranny".

Vučić made his announcement at the headquarters of his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) in the capital Belgrade.

There were celebrations on the streets of the city, with people dancing and chanting "victory", cars honking, and fireworks set off. "Serbia is free," one student told the BBC. "It's a miracle."

The centre of Novi Sad - the northern city that triggered the student-led protests - was crowded. "Everything is going to get better now," David Vasić, one of those celebrating, told the BBC Serbian.

The Student List - which has no obvious leaders and whose members are not used to politics - had attracted anti-government voters across Serbia.

It decided to field candidates to the 250-member parliament from across Serbian society including doctors, actors, academics and sports personalities.

The anti-corruption movement campaigned on a manifesto that included purging officials who broke rules cracking down on protesters, stopping party loyalists from leading public enterprises, and freeing the public broadcaster of political control.

Vučić and the SNS party have repeatedly denied corruption.

Vučić, who backs Serbia's candidacy for the European Union while refusing to impose sanctions on Russia over its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, had pledged to increase pensions and public sector salaries, and investment in state healthcare.

Preliminary figures provided by Serbia's election commission suggested a record high turnout, with 64.9% having cast their vote by 18:00 local time (17:00 GMT), two hours before polls were set to close.

Earlier in the day, long queues were seen outside polling stations in cities and towns across Serbia.

This was also the case outside booths in number of countries with sizeable Serbian communities - including Slovenia's capital Ljubljana, Germany's Munich, and Los Angeles and Chicago in the US.

In France, Serbian voters waited in line in heavy rain in Paris.

The election was held amid high tensions across Serbia, with police sealing off streets around the Republic Electoral Commission (RIK) in Belgrade.

articles.title: After 65+ years of family ranching, Florida approved a $12.9 million easement to permanently protect 5,610 acres of Hendrie Ranch while cattle, hay and timber operations continue
articles.summary: A 5,610-acre stretch of a multigenerational Florida ranch will remain protected from future development after state officials approved a $12.9 million
articles.body: A 5,610-acre stretch of a multigenerational Florida ranch will remain protected from future development after state officials approved a $12.9 million conservation easement. Details from the Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services (FDACS), Florida Department of Environmental Protection records and the Florida Wildlife Corridor Foundation show the agreement will preserve Hendrie Ranch while allowing its agricultural operations to continue. The Hendrie Ranch easement was approved by Florida’s Governor and Cabinet on December 17, 2024, as part of the state’s Rural and Family Lands Protection Program. The protected parcel covers approximately 5,610.26 acres in Highlands County, along U.S. Highway 27 near Venus, with the state paying $12.9 million for the conservation easement. State records put the purchase price at about $2,300 per acre. The arrangement does not turn the ranch into a public preserve or end its agricultural use. Instead, the easement limits future development while the Hendrie family can continue using the land for cattle, hay production and timber harvesting. The ranch has been managed by the family for more than 65 years, with the property supporting a working beef operation alongside forests, wetlands and native Florida habitat.A working ranch inside a major wildlife corridorHendrie Ranch sits on the eastern slope of the southern Lake Wales Ridge and forms part of the Florida Wildlife Corridor, a network intended to connect important natural areas across the state. The property contains a mix of improved and native pasture, pine flatwoods, scrub, wetland forests and seasonal wetlands. State documents indicate that roughly 48% of the 5,610-acre easement area is wetlands, while the remainder includes uplands and agricultural areas.The ranch is also connected to a broader conservation landscape, sitting near several protected properties and the Archbold Biological Station. The Florida Wildlife Corridor Foundation notes that the ranch supports about 600 beef cattle and has been used for scientific research.Its habitat is significant for a range of wildlife. Records identify species including the Florida scrub-jay, sandhill crane, Florida mouse and Sherman’s fox squirrel, alongside Florida black bears. The property also provides habitat within a landscape important for species such as the Florida panther.Protection without ending ranchingThe Hendrie transaction is part of Florida’s broader effort to keep agricultural land from being converted to residential or other development while maintaining working farms and ranches.The Rural and Family Lands Protection Program, established in 2001, uses conservation easements to protect agricultural properties while allowing landowners to continue farming, ranching and forestry. The December 2024 approvals represented a major expansion of the state’s protected working-land portfolio.Hendrie Ranch has actually been part of Florida’s conservation efforts before this latest agreement. A separate 663-acre portion of the ranch received protection through a conservation easement approved in 2022. That earlier project was also tied to the Florida Wildlife Corridor and Lake Wales Ridge conservation landscape.With the latest 5,610-acre easement, a substantial additional portion of the family ranch is now shielded from future development while cattle continue to graze the pastures and the property remains an active agricultural and timber operation.The result is a model increasingly being used across Florida: keeping privately owned land economically productive while permanently limiting the kind of development that could fragment its farms, forests and wildlife habitat.You use AI every day. articles.summary: Kristen Stewart’s Malibu home brought together contemporary architecture, Pacific Ocean views and an unconventional design feature that set it apart from
articles.body: Kristen Stewart’s Malibu home brought together contemporary architecture, Pacific Ocean views and an unconventional design feature that set it apart from the typical celebrity retreat. Purchased in 2011 with her mother, Jules Mann-Stewart, the property remained associated with the Twilight star for more than a decade before selling for $8.3 million in 2022. Architectural Digest, which reported on both the home’s original listing and its eventual sale, documented the property’s distinctive layout and its journey through the luxury real estate market. According to Architectural Digest and Mansion Global, the five-bedroom residence was initially listed for $9.5 million in August 2020. The asking price was subsequently reduced, and the property eventually changed hands in late May 2022 for $8.3 million, falling short of its original asking price but substantially exceeding its 2011 purchase price.A modern home with an unusual architectural featureLocated in Malibu’s Latigo Beach community, the approximately 5,800-square-foot property was designed by Los Angeles-based architect Lorcan O’Herlihy. Built in 1993, the contemporary residence combined glass-and-steel construction with expansive windows, multiple levels and an emphasis on indoor-outdoor living. One of its most distinctive elements was a separate, oval-shaped, two-storey guesthouse connected to the main residence by a suspension bridge. The unusual arrangement gave the property an architectural identity beyond its ocean views, while creating a degree of separation between the main living quarters and the guest accommodation.The guesthouse featured its own living space, kitchenette, bedroom and bathroom. The main house contained the remaining bedrooms and bathrooms, along with shared living and entertaining areas. Architectural Digest’s original 2020 report highlighted the bridge as a defining feature of the property, while Observer’s coverage of the listing also detailed the unusual connection between the two structures.Ocean views and indoor-outdoor livingAlthough the home was not directly on the sand, its location offered access to the beach and views of the Pacific Ocean. The upper-level deck provided one of the property’s most appealing vantage points, while glass doors opened the interior spaces towards outdoor balconies.Inside, the home featured an open living and dining area, a fireplace and a modern kitchen with wooden cabinetry and stainless-steel appliances. The layout was spread across multiple levels, with staircases connecting the different parts of the residence.Outdoor spaces included landscaped terraces, secluded patios and a spa area. The combination of private outdoor retreats and expansive glazing gave the property a relaxed coastal character without sacrificing the contemporary design associated with high-end Malibu homes.From a $9.5 million listing to an $8.3 million saleThe Malibu property first entered the market in August 2020 with an asking price of $9.5 million, nearly double its original purchase price. By April 2022, the home had been relisted for $8.5 million, according to Mansion Global. It ultimately sold for $8.3 million in May that year, bringing its time on the market to nearly two years.The final sale price represented a $3.5 million increase over the reported $4.8 million purchase price in 2011, before accounting for ownership costs, maintenance, taxes and any improvements made to the home. The sale also marked the end of a long chapter for the property, which had been linked to Stewart and her mother since the early years of the actor’s rise to international fame through the Twilight franchise.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Further, EROs decide on the inclusion/exclusion of an elector on the basis of facts and records.” An EC official said software and algorithm details were conventionally not shared under RTI requests. Even EVM manufacturers like Bharat Electronics Ltd and Electronics Corporation of India Ltd have earlier refused to share EVM source codes while replying to RTI queries.Ayyub had sought to know whether the software or the AI platform automatically flagged records for verification, correction or deletion and if that was the case, what was the detailed workflow followed after such records were identified.He had asked whether any AI, machine learning, predictive analytics, or automated decision support system was used in any stage of the SIR exercise.In response to the queries, EC simply said the information sought was a “clarification which does not come under the information as per Section 2(f) of RTI Act”.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.body: NEW DELHI: From spotting deepfake to questioning a chatbot’s confident but incorrect answers, artificial intelligence (AI) is moving from being an optional subject towards becoming a basic skill for CBSE schoolchildren. Taking a step towards more formal AI teaching in schools, NCERT has developed a 20-hour introductory module for Classes IX-XII, which it has earmarked for school-based assessment. Separate AI textbooks are also being prepared for students pursuing the subject at a more advanced level.The move is part of a wider effort to make AI literacy accessible to students, irrespective of whether they study computers or choose AI as an elective. The idea is to first familiarise children with how the technology works, its uses and limitations, before moving towards more structured teaching through textbooks.NCERT developed the module on computational thinking (CT) and AI in consultation with IIT Madras and IIT Jodhpur.In an April-9 circular, CBSE had announced that NCERT would provide modules for Classes IX-XII for internal assessment during the 2026-27 academic session. Under the board’s revised scheme, CT and AI modules are compulsory for Class IX, while Class X continues under the existing scheme.A senior education ministry official said AI had become an important part of everyday activities, from education and research to content writing and career guidance. “AI tools are being used for studies, research, content writing and even career advice. articles.title: Spotify uploads Irish lyrics for Dolly Parton's Welsh Jolene version
articles.summary: The single is the second posthumous release from Parton - who was of Welsh descent.
articles.body:
The lyrics to Dolly Parton's Welsh version of her hit Jolene were uploaded mistakenly to Spotify in Irish.

The song was recorded before her death on 25 August , and is a collaboration with Welsh singer-songwriter Bronwen Lewis as well as Parton's niece, Jada Star.

The version has parts of the song sung in English and Welsh - but the lyrics presented on the digital audio streaming service Spotify actually showed the language as Irish.

Spotify removed the Irish lyrics after the BBC approached it for comment.

The BBC asked Spotify when the single and lyrics were uploaded, when the error was noticed and when it will be replaced, but did not receive a response.

The single came out on 9 October , and is the second posthumous release from Parton - who was of Welsh descent.

The legendary country artist won 10 Grammy awards, sold more than 100 million records worldwide, and wrote more than 3,000 songs after a career spanning seven decades.

Jolene was released in 1973, and is about the fear she might lose her husband Carl Dean to a red-headed bank clerk who had flirted with him early on in their marriage .

It was was nominated for a Grammy in 1974, gave Parton her second number one single on the Billboard Hot Country Singles chart and her first foray into the main Hot 100 chart (60).

It has since had more than one billion streams on Spotify, and many famous singers have gone on to cover Jolene.

The Welsh version of the song came about after Lewis, from Neath, had translated the country classic and posted it on social media.

Then Star, Parton's niece, reached out and suggested recording Jolene in Welsh with Lewis - and Parton joined too.

In 2008, during a concert at the Cardiff International Arena, Parton reportedly revealed her Welsh ancestry to fans in the crowd.

Star revealed one side of the family from Parton's mother Avie Lee Owens was initially believed to have come from Conwy.

Following the singer's death, research by staff at Conwy council's archives suggested Parton's ancestors were from Machynlleth, in Powys, not Conwy as previously thought.

articles.title: Deeply divided Israel braces for pivotal election
articles.summary: After three years of regional war, this is a battle Israel always knew was coming, writes Lucy Williamson.
articles.body:
After three years of regional war, this is a battle Israel always knew was coming.

The general election on Tuesday hangs over a country that's deeply divided and ready for a fight.

Polls published on Friday put the governing coalition and the main opposition bloc almost neck-and-neck, with half a million first-time voters due to cast their ballot and some 70,000 Israelis reportedly flying in from abroad specifically to vote.

On Saturday night, vast crowds of opposition voters gathered in central Tel Aviv to demand a change of government.

"We're optimistic," 21-year-old Omri told me. "I want peace, I want security, and I want to end corruption and get the religious fanatics out."

This campaign has been energized by new tactics - including AI videos designed to grab the headlines - and also by a new face.

Gadi Eisenkot is, perhaps, not the man you might expect to take on the flashy, aggressive, media-savvy brand of Israel's longest-serving prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu.

How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

Israel's far right find fertile ground among first-time voters

The bitter row over military service that could shape Israel's future

Relatively new to politics, with a working-class Moroccan background, Eisenkot is a former military chief of staff who is renowned for his calm manner and low-drama approach. He's been dubbed by some as a "non-politician".

But he and his centrist Yashar party have regularly pipped Netanyahu and his Likud party to the top spot in recent polls, the last of which was published on Friday, in line with Israeli election law.

Israeli politics is the art of coalition-building, rather than the task of any one party winning power, but with the predicted result too close to call, Eisenkot's rising profile has sharpened a race many Israelis already see as existential for the future of their country.

I watched him slip past the cameras at a community centre for Ethiopian Jews in the city of Ramle last week, through a gaggle of security personnel and advisors.

One of those who had come to hear him speak was David, a smartly dressed man in a freshly-pressed shirt and navy jacket, who said he had met Eisenkot before.

"He looks you in the eye, not like a leader looking down at someone," David told me. "And he listens. He's very sympathetic."

Eisenkot's appeal is often put down to his personal manner and profile. A softly-spoken military man whose son was killed during the Gaza War, he has presented himself as coming "from the periphery", not from Israel's wealthy urban elite.

His Moroccan background became election headlines earlier this month when a pro-Netanyahu speaker used a racist slur to refer to Eisenkot during a TV debate, referring to him as a Moroccan "monkey".

"These elections are about many issues," Eisenkot told the crowd gathered at the Ramle community centre. "They are about security, economy, education...but primarily, they are about the identity of the State of Israel, and what kind of Israel we want to see. A Jewish state, a democratic state, a liberal, tolerant, egalitarian state."

This is music to opposition ears, who say Benjamin Netanyahu's government is a threat to Israel's democracy, pointing to his efforts to curb the powers of the judicial system, and his refusal to establish a state commission of inquiry into the 7 October 2023 attacks on the grounds that the country's Supreme Court would be biased against him.

Eisenkot, along with other opposition leaders, has attempted to draw voters away from Netanyahu's right-wing Likud party by promising such a state inquiry, which a recent survey suggests is supported by more than 70% of Jewish Israelis.

He has also vowed to enforce court rulings on drafting ultra-Orthodox Jews into national military service - another measure that is popular with right-wing voters and opposition alike.

Benjamin Netanyahu has hit back with a campaign focused on Israel's security, and a core campaign slogan of "No Surrender".

He has repeatedly cast his rivals as soft on security, playing on the fears of some right-wing voters that Jewish opposition parties might ally with Israel's Arab parties to secure a majority, and suggesting this could compromise national security.

Around one-fifth of Israel's population is Arab - many of whom describe themselves as Palestinian citizens of Israel.

These are the first elections since the 7 October attacks, in which Hamas-led gunmen stormed through Gaza's border fence, killing almost 1,200 people and taking 251 hostage.

It was Israel's worst security failure, but three years on its prime minister is again running for re-election as the only man who can keep Israel safe.

"If the army had woken him in time, it wouldn't have happened," Shlomi Bashar told me, one of several die-hard Netanyahu fans drinking in a basement café in Jerusalem's Mahane Yehuda market. "He does bear a certain responsibility, but after the 7 October, he changed the entire Middle East."

Netanyahu has been hammering home the message that Israel's wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran, in the years after the 7 October attacks, have reduced existential threats to the country.

"We need him to be re-elected so that he can finish this work," said Shlomi. "In my opinion, he is one of the best leaders in the world. Most of the world loves him and respects him, because he is a strong man and his ideas are correct."

The prime minister has traditionally relied on a stable base of right-wing voters, but is projected to see a thinning of support in this election. Some voters may be slipping away to opposition parties like Eisenkot's. Others, including some die-hard Likud voters we spoke to, said the 7 October attacks had pushed them towards parties further on the right.

Lt Col (Res) Eyal Hajbi, head of the regional civil defence unit in the Netanyahu stronghold of Sderot, right on the Gaza border, lost several friends and colleagues in the attacks. He lights candles for them every day in his office, and told me he would be thinking about them when he cast his ballot on Tuesday.

Standing on a ridge overlooking the ruins of northern Gaza, he gestured to the wasteland where Israel's army has completely flattened the neighbourhoods of Beit Lahia and Beit Hanoun.

"As far as I'm concerned, after 7 October, we should wipe them all out," he said. "I've changed my understanding of Gaza. Before, I wouldn't have said we should destroy it."

He told me he and his family had always voted Likud, but that now he was voting for the far-right party of Itamar Ben Gvir, Jewish Power.

"My family has become more extreme than it ever was before," he said. "If once we deliberated over it, today we don't think twice; we vote."

Polls suggest that less than 10% of Israelis are undecided and that very few of those are considering switching between government parties and opposition ones.

Ben Gvir, National Security minister in Netanyahu's coalition, has been reaching out to younger voters through headline-grabbing social media campaigns.

A poll for one of Israel's leading newspapers, Yedioth Ahronoth, published on 9 October, suggested that more than 16% of first-time voters in Israel would choose far-right parties like his.

In Sderot, a group of 18 year olds from a nearby Jewish religious college told me their political views had been affected by the 7 October attacks far more than their parents. All four teenagers were planning to vote for another far-right party, Religious Zionism, led by Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich.

"Today, the whole younger generation understands that peaceful paths will not work," Aviad Elmahach, one of the teenagers, told me. "Older adults, who are set in a fixed mindset, find [it] harder to change, but the youth understand that we need to be here with strength and an iron fist, which is the only way to win."

The lesson of 7 October, he said, was that Israel needed to be as forceful as possible in its relations with the Palestinians, more than 74,000 of whom have been killed by Israel in Gaza since then, according to the Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.

"The youth have a fresh new perspective that has not yet become entrenched in politics, and they understand very well why we're voting for Smotrich - it means holding the land with strength and giving [the Palestinians] nothing through peaceful gestures."

A little further south along the Gaza border are the kibbutzim that were overrun by gunmen during the Hamas attacks. They were renowned for decades as bastions of the Israeli left.

Among them is Nir Oz, where 47 people were killed and 76 taken hostage that day.

Three years on, residents are moving back. Twenty-six-year-old Gal Pauker has opened a Friday wine café at the edge of his small vineyard next to the Gaza border - a few wooden tables set out under sheets of beige canvas to shade customers from the strong desert sun. His grandfather Gideon was killed during the 7 October attacks.

I asked Gal, and his mother Galia, whether the those attacks had shifted their political views.

"We need a change - we can't live with this government anymore," Galia said. "And I'm not talking about security, I'm talking first about humanity."

Having voted for centrist parties in the past, Galia says she's decided to vote for Eisenkot this time around, because "he's an ordinary guy and I hope he'll continue the way he's talking".

Her son Gal said he was deciding between Eisenkot and the left-leaning Democrats party of Yair Golan, another former army general.

"I'm not naïve. I know there are a lot of more militant voices from young generations," he said. "I don't know if Eisenkot will be better than Golan in terms of security, but I think we have bigger problems: economics, social problems, education, health. We didn't get new neighbours on October 7 - it was a major event, but didn't change how we see ourselves."

Threats to security versus threats to democracy - these are old political tramlines for Israeli voters, deepened by the 7 October attacks, and by four years of the most right-wing government in Israel's history.

But on some of the biggest international concerns, the differences between government and opposition are not as wide as it might seem.

Gadi Eisenkot has pledged to end Hamas rule of Gaza within 18 months, either through a US-led peace plan, or through "military and operational capabilities".

All the main opposition leaders have voiced support for some form of Israeli settlement in the occupied West Bank, which has expanded massively under the current government and is illegal under international law. None have openly committed to the idea of full Palestinian statehood, something Benjamin Netanyahu has vowed to block. Eisenkot has spoken about creating the conditions for "autonomy or state-minus" under ultimate Israeli security control.

Tuesday's vote could well end in deadlock, with neither government nor opposition able to form a majority without the support of Arab parties, which polls project could win enough seats to be kingmakers. All but one of Israel's Jewish opposition parties have so far rejected working with either of the two Arab party blocs.

With Benjamin Netanyahu ramping up warnings of fresh threats from Iran, opposition voices warning of potential disruption to the ballot, and Israeli rights activists warning of a further spike in violence by settlers in the occupied West Bank, political instability at home could leave Israelis facing both a fresh test of their democracy, and fresh security threats.

articles.body: A California mansion built by actor John Stamos during the height of his Full House fame has seen its asking price drop by more than half since it first entered the market in 2025. Located in Calabasas, the Mediterranean-style estate was built in 1992 after Stamos purchased six acres of land in 1991 for $430,000. According to the property’s current listing on Compass, the home is now being offered for approximately $6.4 million, down from its initial asking price of nearly $13 million. The reduction follows extensive renovations by its current owners, who bought the property in 2020 and invested millions in upgrading the house and grounds.From a $430,000 land purchase to a celebrity mansionStamos, best known for playing Jesse Katsopolis on the sitcom Full House, bought the six-acre property in the hills of Calabasas in 1991. Property records cited by Realtor.com show that he paid $430,000 for the land before building the Mediterranean-style residence a year later. The actor owned the home for about a decade, selling it in 2001 for $2.15 million. The property changed hands again over the following years before Justin and Candace Aguilera purchased it in early 2020 for $2.95 million.The Aguileras saw potential in the residence despite its dated interiors. Justin Aguilera told Realtor.com that much of the house had not been updated since the early 1990s, but its underlying design and structure appealed to them. The couple subsequently undertook an extensive renovation of the home and its surrounding grounds, transforming the property into a contemporary luxury estate while retaining its Mediterranean-inspired character.Inside the 7,500-square-foot Calabasas estateThe property at 25665 Mulholland Highway is currently listed on Compass for $6.399 million. The listing describes a gated estate spread across approximately 6.14 acres, with six bedrooms, six bathrooms and about 7,547 square feet of living space. The two-storey residence features soaring ceilings, expansive windows and views of the surrounding mountains and valley. Its interiors combine prominent stonework, designer finishes and statement architectural features.During the renovation, the Aguileras introduced book-matched Panda marble flooring, which features distinctive black patterns against a white background. They also installed a crystal chandelier measuring approximately 15 feet and added a double-sided fireplace to the formal living room. The primary suite is another major feature of the property. When the home was first marketed in 2025, Realtor.com described the suite as approximately 2,500 square feet, with a vaulted-ceiling bedroom, a sitting area with a fireplace, a wet bar, a black-marble bathroom and a dedicated glam room. The house was also designed for entertaining, with bars inside and outside. The indoor bar room features marble flooring, black coffered ceilings and seating for at least six people.Pool, landscaped grounds and fire-safety upgradesThe renovations extended beyond the interiors. The owners replastered the swimming pool, which includes a hot tub and grotto, upgraded approximately 5,000 square feet of patio space with travertine and added 350 landscape lights. They also installed fire-safety measures, including a sprinkler system around the hillside and hardscaped areas. These improvements were intended to address the risks associated with the property's elevated location and surrounding landscape.Large windows were installed to preserve views across Malibu Canyon. Aguilera told Realtor.com that clouds moving in from the coast could settle below the property, creating the impression of a blanket of fog resembling a waterfall. The six-acre setting also offers room for potential future additions. According to Compass, the grounds could provide space for further expansion, including the possibility of a helipad, subject to applicable approvals.Why the asking price has fallen to $6.4 millionIts asking price subsequently changed several times as the property was listed and withdrawn from the market. Compass listing history shows that the home was offered for $7.25 million in December 2025 before being relisted in January 2026 for $6.85 million. Further reductions brought the asking price to $6.599 million in February and $6.399 million in April 2026. The listing remained active in the available September 2026 records. The current asking price is roughly 51% below the original $13 million figure. However, an asking-price reduction does not necessarily establish the property's market value or indicate that a seller has incurred a loss.The Aguileras purchased the estate for $2.95 million in 2020 and reportedly invested more than $3 million in renovations, according to the New York Post. Those expenses, along with ongoing ownership costs and market conditions, form part of the broader financial picture behind the listing. The mansion's price history illustrates the challenges of marketing a highly customised luxury property. Although its acreage, views, extensive upgrades and celebrity connection distinguish it from other homes, finding a buyer willing to meet the original asking price has proved difficult.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.body: NEW DELHI: Urging UN to show leadership, and not remain a mere spectator to global crises, external affairs minister S Jaishankar said Sunday large parts of the world cannot be left out from decision-making. At an event on UN Day, he underlined the need for long-awaited reforms.“We live in an imperfect world but we all continuously strive towards greater perfection. Where UN is concerned, that means recognising its shortcomings and limitations and seeking its improvement. The case for reformed multilateralism gets stronger by the day,” he said.Jaishankar spoke about how countries with little say were paying the price for conflicts in West Asia and Ukraine. He also underscored the threat to peace from terrorism, saying its usage as an instrument of statecraft is simply unacceptable.“It can never be justified; it can never be rationalised. Yet, it continues because not all states really display zero-tolerance. Despite history holding so many lessons, some still allow political calculations to take precedence.”“The world must develop sharper awareness about this common threat. And it must come together with stronger resolve and counter terrorism in all its forms and manifestations,” he added.He said the world cannot advance half-prosperous and half-denied and in an era of intricate supply chains, of globalised markets and of common resources, this is simply a prescription for continuous instability.“The Global South today faces a 4F crisis: of finance, fuel, food, and fertiliser. The Global North must realise it has equal stakes in finding solutions. International economy must be urgently de-risked and nations provided with more diversified options. Market distortions through constriction and choke-points only add to suffering. A genuine dialogue in this regard is overdue,” the minister said.Underlining the significance of AI as the mother of all change, Jaishankar said something so sweeping and consequential cannot be left in the hands of just a few. “That would go counter to the trends of freedom and democratisation that the world has seen over the last eighty years,” he added.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
